RELEVANT CHARACTER BACKGROUND

Aminata Diallo is a young woman from a farming village who left two years ago after a failed harvest. Her eldest uncle had intended for her to go to the city to marry, but she convinced her mother to let her learn a trade; her mother had once seen a woman plastering walls and Aminata said she could do that too. She now works as both a porridge vendor and an apprentice plasterer.

Every morning she wakes at 4:30, prepares millet porridge, and sells it at a construction site gate. She is careful with money, never gives credit even to foremen, and keeps her savings in a tin box hidden under her mattress because she does not trust banks—she witnessed a bank collapse when she was twelve and saw a neighbor lose her funeral savings. She sends a portion of her earnings to pay for her younger sister's school supplies back home.

She attends a government-run trade school where she studies plastering, practicing diligently and photographing her work with a secondhand cellphone to review her technique. She keeps a folder labeled "walls" and makes notes and sketches to correct imperfections. She is methodical and patient, observing instructors and peers closely—Serge, learning plumbing, and Mariam, learning tiling, share her cramped rented room. She helps Mariam with heavy burdens and occasionally shares her porridge with a stray dog, but she is guarded with her words and never reveals her savings or family circumstances.

She values punctuality and self-discipline; she has never missed a class since enrollment and usually leaves the construction site as soon as her pot is empty, following a fixed route to school. When workers have offered her gifts or invitations in the past, she has politely declined and moved on. She speaks in short, measured sentences and is cautious in personal relationships. She is polite but firm in business, smiling while refusing credit.

She knows the young mason's helper only by sight and a nod; he sometimes buys porridge on busy mornings. She has not exchanged more than greetings with him and knows only that he is friendly with other workers.

OBJECTIVE SITUATION

Aminata is packing her empty porridge pot at the construction site gate. A young mason's helper steps closer, holding out a small paper bag of roasted groundnuts. He says, "There's a new tea stall by the market, just ten minutes away. I have a break now—come with me before your class." The afternoon sun is hot. Her trade school starts in under an hour. He waits, smiling, while she adjusts the pot on her head.

PRE-APPRAISAL STATE AND ACCESSIBLE MEMORIES

She is tired from waking at 4:30 and has been standing in the hot sun since early morning. Her cloth pouch of coins is heavy, and she wants a cool drink before class. She calculates that a detour to the tea stall would leave her only a short walk to school. The sight of the groundnuts reminds her of the roasted peanuts her mother packed for her as a child in the village. The tea stall at the market is something she passed yesterday on her way to school, and she noticed its new sign.
